programme.displayName: Amazon SNS: Create, Subscribe, and Publish
programme.subtitle: Beginner Amazon SNS hands-on labs for AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) preparation
programme.description: Update of the SNS Study Tracker programme sns-learning-path. Build and test Amazon SNS publish/subscribe patterns in Europe (London), including standard topics, email confirmation, Amazon SQS fan-out, filtering, raw delivery, Lambda subscriptions, monitoring, encryption, FIFO ordering, delivery failure handling, and architecture decisions.
programme.learningOutcome: Explain when SAA-C03 scenarios call for Amazon SNS; create and publish to standard and FIFO topics; connect subscribers; use SQS fan-out and filtering; monitor delivery; apply encryption; and troubleshoot common subscription, policy, KMS, and delivery failures.

phases.description: Create a dedicated IAM user under an administrator-controlled account, configure a CLI profile, and create the first standard SNS topic.

tasks.title: Create a dedicated IAM user and validate SNS lab access
tasks.feature: IAM user access for SNS training
tasks.goal: Create the fixed IAM user sns-study-tracker-lab-user, sign in without using the root user, configure the AWS CLI for Europe (London), and validate the active identity before running SNS tasks.
tasks.whyItMatters: The root user has unrestricted account access and should not be used for routine labs. On SAA-C03, wording such as least privilege, temporary permissions, separate human access, or avoid root credentials should make you choose IAM identities or roles. For this guided lab, the administrator must grant only the approved SNS, SQS, Lambda, CloudWatch, KMS, and S3 permissions required by the later tasks; application workloads should use IAM roles rather than distributed long-term credentials.

consoleSteps.warning: Use the root user only for account-level administration when necessary; do not use it for SNS lab work.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The user can perform only the approved training actions.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A CLI access key is available only to the learner who created it.
consoleSteps.warning: The secret access key is shown only once. Do not paste it into this Follow Along, source control, chat, or a shared location.

tasks.title: Create and inspect a standard SNS topic
tasks.feature: Amazon SNS standard topic and topic ARN
tasks.goal: Create sns-study-tracker-standard-topic in eu-west-2 and identify its immutable type, name, and ARN.
tasks.whyItMatters: An SNS topic is a logical publish/subscribe channel. SAA-C03 wording such as broadcast one event to multiple independent consumers, push notifications, fan-out, or decouple publishers from subscribers should make SNS a leading answer. Standard topics suit best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery patterns; use FIFO only when strict ordering and deduplication are required.

consoleSteps.title: Open SNS topics
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Create topic page opens in eu-west-2.

consoleSteps.title: Select standard delivery
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The topic is configured as a standard topic.
consoleSteps.warning: Topic type cannot be changed after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Set the topic name
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The fixed harmless topic name is entered.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not include personal, confidential, or sensitive data in topic names.

consoleSteps.title: Create the topic
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The topic details page displays sns-study-tracker-standard-topic and its ARN.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the Topic ARN returned here in later commands.

cliSteps.command: aws sns create-topic --name sns-study-tracker-standard-topic --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the standard SNS topic and returns its TopicArn.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the TopicArn for sns-study-tracker-standard-topic.
cliSteps.warning: Save the returned TopicArn as the earlier-command output used by subsequent SNS commands.

cliSteps.command: aws sns get-topic-attributes --topic-arn "<TopicArn returned by the preceding create-topic command>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Reads the topic attributes, including the topic policy and subscription counters.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an Attributes object for the topic.
cliSteps.warning: Replace only the TopicArn with the output from the immediately preceding create-topic command.

verification.title: Confirm the topic ARN
verification.instruction: Open the topic Details page or inspect the create-topic response.
verification.expectedResult: The ARN identifies the sns service, eu-west-2, the account, and sns-study-tracker-standard-topic.

cleanup.title: Retain for later tasks
cleanup.instruction: Do not delete sns-study-tracker-standard-topic until the programme final cleanup.
cleanup.description: Do not delete sns-study-tracker-standard-topic until the programme final cleanup.
cleanup.verification: The topic remains available for the subscription and publishing tasks.

tasks.title: Publish a harmless message and confirm an email subscription
tasks.feature: SNS publishing, email confirmation, and subscription state
tasks.goal: Publish a test message and create an email subscription that the learner explicitly confirms from a mailbox they control.
tasks.whyItMatters: SNS accepts a publish request and attempts delivery to each confirmed subscription. Email endpoints require confirmation. On SAA-C03, a pending confirmation state explains why an email recipient did not receive notifications; it is not a topic-publish failure.

consoleSteps.title: Start the email subscription

instructions.text: Enter an email address you control.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subscription is created with PendingConfirmation status.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only a mailbox you are authorized to access.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm the endpoint
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The browser confirms the subscription and SNS changes the subscription state to Confirmed.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not confirm a subscription for a mailbox you do not control.

consoleSteps.title: Publish the test message

instructions.text: Enter study-tracker standard topic test message.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS accepts the message and the confirmed email endpoint receives a notification.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not publish confidential data.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect the subscription
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subscription details show Confirmed status and the topic ARN.
consoleSteps.warning: Unconfirmed subscriptions do not receive published notifications.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --protocol email --notification-endpoint "<Email address you control>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates an email subscription. SNS sends a confirmation message to the specified endpoint.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains SubscriptionArn with pending confirmation until the recipient confirms it.
cliSteps.warning: The endpoint value is intentionally learner-supplied because email confirmation requires a mailbox the learner controls.

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --subject "Study Tracker SNS test" --message "study-tracker standard topic test message" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publishes a harmless message to the standard topic.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains MessageId, indicating SNS accepted the publish request.
cliSteps.warning: A MessageId does not make an unconfirmed email subscription deliverable.

cliSteps.command: aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Lists the topic subscriptions and their current subscription ARNs or confirmation state.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows the email endpoint and its subscription status.
cliSteps.warning: Replace the TopicArn only with the earlier task output.

verification.title: Confirm delivery readiness
verification.instruction: Confirm that the email subscription is Confirmed before using it as a delivery test.
verification.expectedResult: The subscription is no longer pending confirmation.

verification.title: Confirm publication acceptance
verification.instruction: Review the MessageId returned from publish or the notification received by the confirmed mailbox.
verification.expectedResult: SNS accepted the harmless test message.

cleanup.title: Remove the email subscription if no longer needed
cleanup.instruction: Select only the lab email subscription and choose Delete.
cleanup.description: Select only the lab email subscription and choose Delete.
cleanup.verification: The subscription no longer appears for sns-study-tracker-standard-topic.

tasks.title: Build SNS to SQS fan-out with independent consumers
tasks.goal: Create two separate SQS queues and subscribe them to the standard SNS topic so billing and inventory can process the same order event independently.
tasks.whyItMatters: SNS fan-out pushes one published event to multiple subscribers. Adding one SQS queue per consumer makes each consumer durable and independently scalable during traffic spikes. On SAA-C03, choose SNS plus SQS when several systems need the same event and each system needs its own buffer and retry behavior; do not use a single shared queue when each consumer must receive every event.

consoleSteps.title: Create the billing queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The billing SQS queue exists in eu-west-2.
consoleSteps.warning: The lab identity needs SQS queue-creation permission.

consoleSteps.title: Create the inventory queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The inventory SQS queue exists in eu-west-2.
consoleSteps.warning: Use a separate queue because each consumer needs its own copy of the event.

consoleSteps.title: Subscribe the billing queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The billing queue becomes an SNS subscription.
consoleSteps.warning: SNS must be allowed by the queue resource policy to send messages to the queue.

consoleSteps.title: Subscribe the inventory queue
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The inventory queue becomes an SNS subscription.
consoleSteps.warning: Review the queue policy after subscription creation to confirm it authorizes the intended SNS topic only.

consoleSteps.title: Publish an order event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS sends a copy of the message to both subscribed queues.
consoleSteps.warning: The queues retain messages until a consumer deletes them or they expire.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name sns-study-tracker-billing-queue --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the billing consumer's standard queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the billing QueueUrl.
cliSteps.warning: Save the QueueUrl output for queue inspection.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name sns-study-tracker-inventory-queue --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the inventory consumer's standard queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the inventory QueueUrl.
cliSteps.warning: An SNS-to-SQS subscription requires a queue policy that permits the specific topic to send messages.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --protocol sqs --notification-endpoint "<BillingQueueArn returned by an SQS get-queue-attributes command>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the billing queue subscription after the queue policy allows the topic to send messages.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the billing SubscriptionArn.
cliSteps.warning: Use the SQS queue ARN, not its QueueUrl, as the endpoint.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --protocol sqs --notification-endpoint "<InventoryQueueArn returned by an SQS get-queue-attributes command>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Creates the inventory queue subscription after the queue policy allows the topic to send messages.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the inventory SubscriptionArn.
cliSteps.warning: An incorrect queue ARN or a queue policy that omits the SNS topic causes delivery failure.

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --message "order-1001-created" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publishes one harmless order event for fan-out testing.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: This verifies publication acceptance; inspect each queue to verify independent delivery.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs receive-message --queue-url "<BillingQueueUrl returned by the billing create-queue command>" --max-number-of-messages 1 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Receives one message from the billing queue without deleting it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an SNS-wrapped message when raw message delivery is disabled.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete the message until the raw-delivery task explains the difference.

verification.title: Verify independent fan-out
verification.instruction: Inspect both queues after publishing order-1001-created.
verification.expectedResult: Each queue has an independently delivered copy of the event.

verification.title: Check the queue access policy
verification.instruction: Review each queue resource policy and confirm it permits only the intended SNS topic to send messages.
verification.expectedResult: The queue policy has an SNS principal and is restricted to the lab topic.

cleanup.title: Retain fan-out resources
cleanup.instruction: Keep the two queues and subscriptions until the filtering and raw-delivery tasks are complete.
cleanup.description: Keep the two queues and subscriptions until the filtering and raw-delivery tasks are complete.
cleanup.verification: Both queues remain subscribed to the standard topic.

tasks.title: Route only relevant events with message attributes and subscription filtering
tasks.feature: SNS message attributes, filter policies, and filter-policy scope
tasks.goal: Configure a subscription filter so the billing queue receives only messages whose eventType attribute is invoice-created.
tasks.whyItMatters: Filtering moves routing decisions into SNS instead of making every consumer receive and discard every message. On SAA-C03, choose SNS subscription filters when consumers need selected event categories from the same topic. Attribute-based filtering is the default scope; payload-based filtering matches values in the message body. Filter policy changes can take up to 15 minutes to become fully effective.

consoleSteps.title: Open the billing subscription
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subscription edit page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Select the billing subscription, not the inventory subscription.

consoleSteps.title: Set attribute-based filtering
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The billing subscription has an eventType filter policy.
consoleSteps.warning: Allow up to 15 minutes for a changed filter policy to become fully effective.

consoleSteps.title: Publish a matching event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The billing subscription accepts the matching event.
consoleSteps.warning: Use String as the message attribute type.

consoleSteps.title: Publish a nonmatching event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The billing subscription filters out the nonmatching event.
consoleSteps.warning: Other subscriptions without a filter can still receive the event.

cliSteps.command: aws sns set-subscription-attributes --subscription-arn "<BillingSubscriptionArn from Task 4>" --attribute-name FilterPolicy --attribute-value '{"eventType":["invoice-created"]}' --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Sets an attribute-based filter policy on the billing subscription.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: The filter policy must be valid JSON and can take up to 15 minutes to become fully effective.

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --message "invoice-1001-created" --message-attributes '{"eventType":{"DataType":"String","StringValue":"invoice-created"}}' --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publishes an event whose message attribute matches the billing filter policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains MessageId.
cliSteps.warning: A matching filter policy permits delivery only after the policy change has propagated.

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --message "inventory-1001-reserved" --message-attributes '{"eventType":{"DataType":"String","StringValue":"inventory-reserved"}}' --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publishes an event whose attribute does not match the billing filter policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains MessageId, but the billing subscription filters the message out.
cliSteps.warning: Publication success does not mean every subscription receives the message.

cliSteps.command: aws sns get-subscription-attributes --subscription-arn "<BillingSubscriptionArn from Task 4>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Confirms the configured filter policy and default FilterPolicyScope.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes FilterPolicy and FilterPolicyScope attributes.
cliSteps.warning: MessageAttributes is the default filter-policy scope; use MessageBody only when the policy must match payload content.

verification.title: Confirm targeted routing
verification.instruction: Compare the billing queue contents after the matching and nonmatching publishes.
verification.expectedResult: The billing queue receives the invoice-created event but not the inventory-reserved event.

verification.title: Inspect filtered-out monitoring
verification.instruction: Open CloudWatch SNS topic metrics and locate a filtered-out metric for the topic.
verification.expectedResult: Filtered messages are visible through the SNS filtered-out metrics after metric publication.

cleanup.title: Remove the filter after the test
cleanup.instruction: Edit only the billing subscription and remove its filter policy if later tasks need every message delivered.
cleanup.description: Edit only the billing subscription and remove its filter policy if later tasks need every message delivered.
cleanup.verification: The subscription no longer shows a FilterPolicy attribute.

tasks.title: Compare SNS envelopes with raw message delivery
tasks.goal: Enable raw message delivery for the inventory SQS subscription and compare its payload with the default SNS JSON envelope.
tasks.whyItMatters: By default, an SQS subscriber receives SNS metadata and the original message in an SNS envelope. Raw delivery sends the published payload as-is. On SAA-C03, choose raw delivery when a subscriber requires the original payload and does not need SNS envelope metadata; do not confuse raw delivery with filtering, because filtering works independently.

consoleSteps.title: Open the inventory subscription
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The inventory subscription edit page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Enable raw message delivery
consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS delivers the unwrapped message body to the SQS subscription.
consoleSteps.warning: Raw delivery removes SNS metadata from the SQS message body.

consoleSteps.title: Publish a comparison message
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The inventory queue receives the message as the raw body.
consoleSteps.warning: The billing queue can retain the default SNS envelope if raw delivery remains disabled there.

cliSteps.command: aws sns set-subscription-attributes --subscription-arn "<InventorySubscriptionArn from Task 4>" --attribute-name RawMessageDelivery --attribute-value true --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enables raw message delivery for the inventory SQS subscription.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without output.
cliSteps.warning: Raw delivery is configured per subscription.

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --message "raw-delivery-comparison" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Publishes a harmless message for payload comparison.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains MessageId.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs receive-message --queue-url "<InventoryQueueUrl from Task 4>" --max-number-of-messages 1 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Reads one inventory message to inspect its body.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The received message body is raw-delivery-comparison rather than an SNS JSON envelope.
cliSteps.warning: Receiving a message makes it temporarily invisible; do not delete it unless the lab cleanup requires it.

verification.title: Compare SQS message formats
verification.instruction: Inspect an inventory queue message and compare it with a message received from a subscription that still uses default delivery.
verification.expectedResult: The raw-delivery queue contains the original message body, while default delivery contains SNS metadata around the message.

cleanup.title: Restore default wrapping if needed
cleanup.instruction: Edit only the inventory subscription and clear Enable raw message delivery when later consumers expect SNS metadata.
cleanup.description: Edit only the inventory subscription and clear Enable raw message delivery when later consumers expect SNS metadata.
cleanup.verification: The subscription RawMessageDelivery attribute is false or absent.

tasks.title: Subscribe a Lambda function and compare direct invocation with SNS plus SQS
tasks.feature: SNS to Lambda and durable SNS to SQS to Lambda architecture
tasks.goal: Subscribe an existing lab Lambda function to the standard topic and compare direct SNS invocation with a durable queue-first design.
tasks.whyItMatters: Direct SNS-to-Lambda is appropriate for simple asynchronous fan-out where immediate function invocation is desired. SNS-to-SQS-to-Lambda is preferable when the consumer needs queue buffering, independent retry behavior, or protection from traffic spikes. On SAA-C03, look for downstream throttling, burst absorption, durable independent processing, or replayable queued work to choose SNS plus SQS.

consoleSteps.title: Create the lab Lambda function
consoleSteps.expectedResult: A Lambda function exists for the direct SNS subscription.
consoleSteps.warning: The Lambda execution role must be administrator-approved and should grant only the function's required permissions, such as CloudWatch Logs write access.

consoleSteps.title: Subscribe the function
consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS creates a Lambda subscription and grants SNS permission to invoke the selected function when the Console flow succeeds.
consoleSteps.warning: If function invocation permission is missing, subscription delivery fails.

consoleSteps.title: Publish a Lambda test
consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS invokes the subscribed Lambda function.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not include sensitive data in the test payload.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect function logs
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function's log group contains an invocation corresponding to the SNS test.
consoleSteps.warning: No log output can indicate missing execution-role logging permissions or a function error.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda get-function --function-name sns-study-tracker-handler --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Confirms that the existing Console-created lab function is available before creating an SNS subscription.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the function configuration and ARN.
cliSteps.warning: This task intentionally uses the Console creation flow so no function package, source archive, execution-role ARN, or credentials are embedded in this programme.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda add-permission --function-name sns-study-tracker-handler --statement-id sns-study-tracker-standard-topic-invoke --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal sns.amazonaws.com --source-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Allows only the specified SNS topic to invoke the lab Lambda function.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the added Lambda resource-policy statement.
cliSteps.warning: Use the exact topic ARN from Task 2; a different ARN prevents the intended topic from invoking the function.

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 2>" --protocol lambda --notification-endpoint "<FunctionArn returned by the preceding get-function command>" --region eu-west-2

On SAA-C03, choose an SNS subscription DLQ when a notification endpoint can be temporarily or permanently unavailable and failed notifications require analysis or reprocessing.

tasks.title: Create FIFO ordered fan-out and compare FIFO with standard SNS
tasks.feature: SNS FIFO topic, MessageGroupId, deduplication, and SQS FIFO
tasks.goal: Create an SNS FIFO topic and an SQS FIFO queue, then publish an ordered order-status event using a message group ID and deduplication ID.
tasks.whyItMatters: FIFO topics preserve order within a message group and support deduplication. For strict ordered fan-out, use SNS FIFO with SQS FIFO queues. Standard SNS is the better fit when consumers tolerate best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery. FIFO topics cannot deliver to email, SMS, mobile push, or HTTP/S endpoints because those endpoints cannot preserve strict ordering.

consoleSteps.warning: Use an SQS FIFO queue when strict ordered fan-out is required.

tasks.title: Apply SAA-C03 architecture decisions and troubleshoot SNS delivery
tasks.feature: SNS service selection, access control, cross-account concepts, payload limits, and troubleshooting
tasks.goal: Use a final architecture review to select SNS, SQS, EventBridge, or Kinesis appropriately and diagnose common SNS failures without sending SMS or exposing an HTTP endpoint.
tasks.whyItMatters: SNS is best for real-time pub/sub fan-out to multiple subscribers. SQS is best for persistent pull-based buffering for one consumer group. EventBridge is best for event-rule routing across AWS services and event buses. Kinesis is better for ordered streaming, multiple consumers, and replayable stream processing. SNS messages are limited to 256 KB; for larger payloads, store the payload in S3 and publish an object reference. Cross-account SNS requires identity and resource-based permissions, and encrypted cross-account designs also require KMS authorization.

findings.message: The supplied published programme revision contains no existing task schema beyond three introductory SNS tasks, while the requested update requires SNS, SQS, Lambda, CloudWatch, KMS, S3, IAM, and cross-account behavior. This replacement preserves the exact programme display name and programme identity supplied by the request, while using the required canonical Follow Along package structure.

No IAM policy document is included or proposed. An administrator must apply an organization-approved least-privilege permission set before the learner can create SQS queues, Lambda functions, CloudWatch alarms, or KMS-backed SNS configuration.

The SQS subscription tasks require an SQS queue resource policy that authorizes the specific SNS topic. The policy is deliberately not included because the governing instructions prohibit proposing IAM or resource policies. Validate that the administrator-approved configuration permits only the named source topic.

Cross-account publishing and subscriptions are explained as SAA-C03 design concepts but are not executed because they require a second AWS account and account-specific SNS resource policies, SQS queue policies, IAM permissions, and potentially KMS key-policy changes.

The HTTP/S and SMS topics are covered through safe architecture and troubleshooting guidance rather than execution. Sending SMS can incur charges, and testing HTTP/S delivery requires an endpoint the learner owns and secures.

The S3 oversized-payload task publishes a harmless S3 URI reference only. It does not create an S3 bucket or upload an object because this Follow Along avoids embedding application code, bucket policy documents, or user-specific storage configuration.
